newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Some 40 parties to contest Bulgarian election.
newsitem.headline: Some 40 parties to contest Bulgarian election.

text.p: Some 40 parties and coalitions will take part in Bulgaria's general election on April 19, the Central Electoral Commission said on Wednesday.
A spokeswoman said 57 applications had been received but several parties had since formed coalitions.
Elections were called 20 months ahead of schedule after 30 days of mass protests led by the Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) forced the Bulgarian Socialist Party to stand down.
Opinion polls predict that the UDF, in coalition with smaller parties, will win a majority in the new parliament.

All Bulgaria's political parties have pledged their support for a tough reform programme agreed by the interim cabinet and the International Monetary Fund to stabilise the shattered economy over the next year.

Both President Petar Stoyanov and interim prime minister Stefan Sofianski have warned the measures will be as painful as they are inevitable. Corruption and failure to implement reforms in the past seven years have brought the economy to the brink of collapse.
"Bulgaria's dream factory is already closed, but it's time to open the real factories," Stoyanov said on Tuesday.

Two new parties, the Liberal Democratic Alternative of former president Zhelyu Zhelev and the Euro-Left, which groups several Socialist defectors, have a chance of polling the minimum four percent needed for admission to the assembly.
Some 190 parties have sought registration in the country of 8.4 million people since the end of communist rule in 1989.

The Socialists won elections in December 1994 but lost support as the economy worsened. Their candidate suffered a decisive defeat in 1996 presidential elections won by Stoyanov, who ran on the ticket of the united opposition.
Former prime minister Zhan Videnov, who resigned as premier and Socialist party leader in December, will not be standing.
